## Project Overview

This is a Blender automation and management system that provides a web interface for interacting with Blender through WebSocket connections. The system allows for automated 3D model creation, scene management, and real-time control of Blender instances.


## Core Components

### 1. Web Interface (`blender_web_interface.py`)
- Flask-based web application
- Provides UI for browsing and managing Blender models
- Handles model search and viewing functionality
- Serves as the main user interface for the system

### 2. Blender Agent (`blender_agent/`)
- WebSocket server implementation
- Handles communication between web interface and Blender
- Manages Blender Python script execution
- Provides real-time feedback and control

### 3. 3D Model Generation
- Various scripts for automated 3D model creation:
  - `create_3d_car.py`: Car model generator
  - `create_3d_tree.py`: Tree model generator
  - `create_3d_rings.py`: Rings model generator
- Uses Blender Python API for model creation
- Supports customization through parameters

### 4. Database Integration (`chroma_db/`)
- ChromaDB-based storage system
- Indexes and stores Blender models
- Enables efficient search and retrieval
- Maintains model metadata and relationships

### 5. Code Validation System
- Pre-commit hooks for code quality
- Custom validation rules
- Integration with Developer Guide
- Automated style checking


## Key Features
1. Automated 3D model generation
2. Web-based model management
3. Real-time Blender control
4. Model search and retrieval
5. Code quality enforcement
6. Documentation-driven development


## Development Guidelines
- Follow Python coding standards
- Maintain comprehensive documentation
- Use type hints and docstrings
- Implement proper error handling
- Follow the Developer Guide for architecture decisions

Bericht voorbereiden\n            message = {{\n                "type": "bpy_script",\n                "code": script_code\n            }}\n            \n            # Bericht versturen\n            print("Bericht verzenden...")\n            await websocket.send(json.dumps(message))\n            print("Bericht verzonden, wachten op antwoord...")\n            \n            # Antwoord ontvangen\n            response = await websocket.recv()\n            response_data = json.loads(response)\n            \n            if response_data.get("status") == "ok":\n                print("Script succesvol uitgevoerd in Blender!")\n                print(f"Details: {{response_data.get(\'details\', \'\')}}")\n            else:\n                print(\n    f"Fout bij uitvoeren script: {{response_data.get(\'details\', \'Onbekende fout\')}}")\n                if \'traceback\' in response_data:\n                    print("\nError Traceback:")\n                    print(response_data.get(\'traceback\'))\n                \n    except ConnectionRefusedError:\n        print("Kon geen verbinding maken met de Blender WebSocket server.")\n        print(\n    "Controleer of de server draait met: blender -b -P blender_agent/websocket_server.py")\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f"Fout: {{e}}")\n\ndef main():\n    """\n    Hoofdfunctie die een Blender script genereert en verstuurt\n    """\n    # Hier definieer je je Blender script\n    blender_script = """\nimport bpy\nimport math\n\n# Wis bestaande objecten\nbpy.ops.object.select_all(action=\'SELECT\')\nbpy.ops.object.delete()\n\n# TODO: Voeg hier je eigen Blender code toe\n# Voorbeeld: Maak een kubus\nbpy.ops.mesh.primitive_cube_add(size=2, location=(0, 0, 0))\ncube = bpy.context.active_object\ncube.name = "MijnKubus"\n\n# Sla de scene op\nbpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath="{save_path}")\nprint("Bestand opgeslagen als: {save_file}")\n"""\n\n    # Voer het script uit\n    # Voor Windows compatibiliteit\n    if sys.platform == \'win32\':\n        asyncio.set_event_loop_policy(asyncio.WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy())\n        \n    asyncio.run(send_bpy_script(blender_script))\n\nif __name__ == "__main__":\n    main()\n'
